source.description: The citation the address is read from.

PlaybookChange.description:
The change a person makes in the source system themselves: the Workbench never
writes BC, the Portal or MC (``writes`` is 0).
PlaybookChange.title: PlaybookChange

PlaybookEmail.description:
A drafted message to the record's outside party (never sent here: it goes only
through ``/api/actions/preview`` and your confirm, ``card_id`` = the playbook's id).
PlaybookEmail.title: PlaybookEmail

PlaybookTeams.description: A drafted Teams note to the record's internal owner, when the ontology knows them.
PlaybookTeams.title: PlaybookTeams

due.description: The due date and its basis; omitted when none is decided or its value is not this reader's to open.

hidden_steps.description: Steps in places this reader can't open: counted, never named.
hidden_steps.title: Hidden Steps

may_hide_more.description: A source this reader can't fully read may hold more steps (not counted).
may_hide_more.title: May Hide More

state.description: plx.process lateness state: late, on_time, not_due, undetermined, not_applicable.
state.title: State

vendor_number.description: The order number the supplier knows (a FileMaker-era order's FileMaker PO number), when every copy holds one; omitted otherwise.

verdict.description: The verdict and its rule in one sentence.
verdict.title: Verdict

ProactiveSuggestion.description:
One record that needs attention: what we noticed, how we know, what to do and a
draft message (never sent).
ProactiveSuggestion.title: ProactiveSuggestion

ProductMargin.description: One item's margin over the customer's checked order lines of the period.

complete.description: False: an invoiced order without a checked margin carries the item, or not every order was read; the figures cover the checked orders only.
complete.title: Complete

unit_cost_range.description: Lowest to highest booked unit cost over those orders.
unit_cost_range.title: Unit Cost Range

ProductMargin.title: ProductMargin

ProfitDriver.description: One reason a customer's margin is what it is, over its checked orders only.

amount.description: Its effect on the margin, signed.

established.description: False: not established from the records (the text says so and ``where_it_would_live`` where it would be read); no figure is stated.
established.title: Established

sources.description: The cited records this reader may open.
sources.title: Sources

text.description: The reason in one plain sentence; every figure in it is ``amount`` or a checked order's own.
text.title: Text

ProfitDriver.title: ProfitDriver

drivers.description: Why the customer makes or loses money (losing orders, low-margin items, credits; discounts and freight said as not established), over the checked orders only, one currency each.
drivers.title: Drivers

margin_basis.description: What every margin here covers: item ledger cost only (BC books no labour or overhead).
margin_basis.title: Margin Basis

margin_note.description: The plain line saying what the margin basis leaves out.
margin_note.title: Margin Note

next_action.description: A suggested next step from the facts only.

orders_counted.description: Orders whose margin is complete; the totals cover these only.
orders_counted.title: Orders Counted

orders_excluded.description: Orders of the period not yet invoiced: excluded, never blocking.
orders_excluded.title: Orders Excluded

orders_in_period_exact.description: False: orders_in_period is a lower bound.
orders_in_period_exact.title: Orders In Period Exact

orders_more.description: Orders read but not listed (the list stops at 30).
orders_more.title: Orders More

orders_read.description: Orders read; fewer than orders_in_period means no customer total is stated.
orders_read.title: Orders Read

period.description: The period in words, e.g. 'the last 12 months'.
period.title: Period

period_basis.description: How an order counts in the period.
period_basis.title: Period Basis

products.description: Margin per item over the checked orders, worst first.
products.title: Products

ranking.description: What the ranking covers, e.g. 'partial: worst of the 60 most recent orders; 214 more in the period not read'.
ranking.title: Ranking

test_records_hidden.description: How many test or placeholder records were left out, in words ('2 test records hidden'); null for none.
test_records_hidden.title: Test Records Hidden

verdict.description: Stated only when every invoiced order of the period has a checked margin; null otherwise.
verdict.title: Verdict

withheld_orders.description: Orders whose figures you may not read: a count only, never named.
withheld_orders.title: Withheld Orders

PromiseLine.description:
One order line the supplier promised its own date, matched on firm evidence (the
line's item code or description), with its verdict against that date.

days_late.description: Days past the supplier's promised date (late only).
days_late.title: Days Late

matched_by.description: How the confirmation's item was matched to the line: item_code or description.
matched_by.title: Matched By

source.description: The confirmation that promised the line its date.

state.description: Against the supplier's date for this line: late (open past it), not_due, on_time, received (its receipt date unread), undetermined, or not_judged (a lead).
state.title: State

PromiseLine.title: PromiseLine

Proposal.description:
A follow-up draft (email text the person edits, copies or opens in their own mail
client) or a proposed record update. Never sent and never applied by the Workbench.

body.description: The draft text; every date and figure in it is one of ``figures``.
body.title: Body

contact_note.description: Where the address was found, or that no contact was found.
contact_note.title: Contact Note

missing.description: What the draft could not state from the records, in words.
missing.title: Missing

sent.description: Always false: the Workbench never sends or writes; the person does.
sent.title: Sent

to.description: The recipient's address, only when a cited source this reader may open states it and the people directory clears it; null when unknown.
to.title: To

Proposal.title: Proposal

ProposedChange.description:
A record field the evidence shows is out of date: before, after and why. The person
applies it in the system named; the Workbench writes nothing.

evidence.description: The message or document that states the new value.

field.description: The field, in words, e.g. 'Expected receipt date'.
field.title: Field

ProposedChange.title: ProposedChange

handle.description: The L1 citation handle (graph-mail://, api://, bc://, ...).
handle.title: Handle

label.description: Short human label, e.g. 'BC purchase order 90412'.
label.title: Label

open_url.description: Opens the source for this reader; null when it cannot be opened.
open_url.title: Open Url

quote.description: The exact quoted passage, when text.
quote.title: Quote

SourceView.description:
One cited source opened for this reader (``open_url`` of a Source is the app page
``/source?handle=<handle>``, which reads this). Not found reads the same as no access.

access_label.description: 'Viewing with full-read access' when served under the reader's declared full-read grant.
access_label.title: Access Label

SourceView.title: SourceView

SuggestionDraft.description:
A message a person may copy, edit and send themselves: worded only from cited values
this reader may open, never from a message's text. Never sent by the Workbench.

facts.description: Each stated fact and its source.
facts.title: Facts

SuggestionDraft.title: SuggestionDraft

answer.description: ETA confirmed by the vendor? Unknown states are 'unknown', never yes.
answer.title: Answer

when.description: The vendor's confirmed date (yes only, and only beside a source you can open).
when.title: When

amount_suspect.description: Why the total looks wrong in the source: never ranked by.
amount_suspect.title: Amount Suspect

days_at_risk.description: The worst customer order's days at risk (a lower bound).
days_at_risk.title: Days At Risk

Suggestions.description:
What needs your attention and what to do about it, ranked by impact (customer
orders held up, money within its currency, days late); every other open finding is
counted by type. Suggestions only: nothing is sent or written.

collapsed.description: Open findings of other types (no drafted action), counted per type.
collapsed.title: Collapsed

stale_since.description: Set when the server could not read this page in time and serves the last page it read for this same reader: when that page was read (ISO). It is refreshed in the background.
stale_since.title: Stale Since

total.description: Records with a suggestion (all, not only shown).
total.title: Total

Suggestions.title: Suggestions

reason.description: The typed gap, e.g. assembly_order_not_linked_to_order_line, line_item_not_recorded, link_lead_only.
reason.title: Reason

state.description: absent_in_source (the reader's walk was complete), unknown, or note (a count stated for completeness, e.g. POs already received or closed).
state.title: State

at.description: When it happened (ISO date or time), as the cited record states it; null when the record carries no date.
at.title: At

check.description: How the step was checked: read_from_record (a value read from the cited record as this reader), lead (a machine-read reference, e.g. a message naming the PO), computed_from_cited_records (the verdict), text_match (a message or file naming the record by text), not_established (a why verdict no record states), unchecked, or the answer gate's check of a claim.
check.title: Check

sender.description: A message's sender, only when the people exclusion decides it may be shown.
sender.title: Sender

source.description: The record or message the step cites; open_url opens it for this reader. Null only for a verdict that states no date (undetermined).

title.description: What happened, e.g. 'Vendor confirmed delivery by 2026-07-02'; every date and figure in it is a cited value.
title.title: Title

TruthFlag.description:
The latest cross-system truth check (``operating.truth_check``): how many of the
open claims the engine makes the other systems' evidence contradicts.

contradicted.description: Every open claim contradicted by evidence.
contradicted.title: Contradicted

detectors_incomplete.description: Detectors whose latest run did not complete (their claims are partly checked).
detectors_incomplete.title: Detectors Incomplete

late_claims.description: Purchase orders claimed late (past their need date), one per order; unconfirmed orders not yet due are not counted.
late_claims.title: Late Claims

late_contradicted.description: Of those, the orders contradicted by evidence in another system (received, cancelled, a test record, a draft twin, or a need date that is a default).
late_contradicted.title: Late Contradicted

stale.description: The check is older than TRUTH_MAX_AGE (2 hours): its counts are not stated in the label.
stale.title: Stale

TruthFlag.title: TruthFlag

VendorPromise.description:
The order against the date the supplier promised, beside our requested-by verdict
and never in its place. ``link`` confirmed: a firm link joins the confirmation to the
order; unconfirmed_link: a lead whose dates are stated and never judged.

complete.description: False: a later promise this reader cannot see may exist.
complete.title: Complete

days_late.description: Days past the supplier's promised date (late only).
days_late.title: Days Late

lines_hidden.description: Promised lines whose confirmation this reader can't open: counted, never named.
lines_hidden.title: Lines Hidden

measured_against.description: today: the order is open; received: its last receipt.
measured_against.title: Measured Against

per_line.description: The supplier promised each item its own date; lines lists the matched lines.
per_line.title: Per Line

source.description: The confirmation that states the promised date.

VendorPromise.title: VendorPromise

VerdictEvent.description:
The answer's first line, sent the moment the answer gate accepts it (before the
full answer): only what that decision passed, every citation decided for the reader.
VerdictEvent.title: VerdictEvent

about.description: The followed record, or a rule's subject or the record its count is grouped by.

changes.description: Only values whose markings you hold.
changes.title: Changes

counted.description: A windowed rule: the changes counted, every one on a record you may open.
counted.title: Counted

readable.description: False when your grant no longer admits the record: it stays followed and tells you nothing until it does.
readable.title: Readable

watching_since.description: When the incremental pass first read it; null: not yet.
watching_since.title: Watching Since

object_id.description: The record's id, as its page states it.
object_id.title: Object Id

label.description: A label from the record's unmarked name or number; null when it has none.
label.title: Label

WatchRuleDraft.description: The compiled rule shown back for confirmation; nothing is kept.

description.description: What the rule will do, in plain words.
description.title: Description

digest.description: Send it back with the spec to confirm this very rule.
digest.title: Digest

markings.description: The markings the figures it reads carry.
markings.title: Markings

WatchRuleDraft.title: WatchRuleDraft

WatcherItemStateRequest.description:
Dismiss or snooze one item the AI watcher flagged in your briefing; ``open`` undoes
either. Only your own briefing changes; nothing is sent.

until.description: A snooze's last day (YYYY-MM-DD, after today); absent: a week from today.
until.title: Until

WatcherItemStateRequest.title: WatcherItemStateRequest

Watchlist.description:
Your follows, your alert rules and your alerts, newest first, as your grant shows
them now.
Watchlist.title: Watchlist

info.description: Read-only Workbench API for the web app. Every route but auth/config, auth/dev-login and health needs a signed-in reader. Errors are {error:{code,message}}.
info.title: PLX Workbench app API

post.description:
Do the action you previewed, as yourself, once per idempotency key; recorded in
the append-only actions journal. A message goes from your own mailbox only when
sending is enabled and permitted; otherwise it is recorded as a dry run that names
what is missing.

get.description: Your confirmed actions, newest first, from the actions journal.

post.description:
One action on one of your suggestion cards, as it would be done: the exact final
payload (to, cc, subject, body, the message it replies to), the Graph request, the
cited facts it still states, what blocks it and what a live send lacks. Nothing is
done.

get.description: Each of your cards' latest action by you (sent, dry run, failed, done, ...).

One alert's ready-to-use next steps, worded from its own cited sources as you
read them: a drafted email to the supplier or customer, a Teams note to the record's
owner, links to the record here and in its source system, the change to make in the
source system yourself, and snooze / assign / mark handled. Nothing is sent or
written: its actions go through ``/api/actions/*`` (card id = its ``id``) and your
confirm.

post.description: Ask a question; the answer streams as server-sent events.

200.description: Server-sent events. Each event's `event:` is its name and `data:` one JSON object: understanding (UnderstandingEvent), status (StatusEvent: a plain-words progress step), sources (SourcesEvent), verdict (VerdictEvent: the answer's first line once the answer gate accepts it), token (TokenEvent), answer (AnswerPayload, last), error (ErrorBody, last).

get.description: Public: how to sign in (identifiers only).

post.description: Dev and mock modes only: open a demo session (HttpOnly cookie).
Ends a dev session (Entra sign-out is the front end's MSAL logout).

get.description:
Calendar events in the next 14 days you may read, soonest first, each with the
link to its meeting prep brief.

The weekly ops review: orders booked, shipped and invoiced, on-time shipping, late
purchase orders, top alerts, cash position and margin (finance), quality holds, each
weekly figure against the week before. Generated from the records you may read, no
model call; every figure cites its sources and nothing hidden is counted.

parameters.description: Any day of the week (Monday to Sunday); default: last week
parameters.name: week

schema.description: Any day of the week (Monday to Sunday); default: last week
schema.title: Week

get.description:
The meeting prep brief for a calendar event or meeting (its customers and
suppliers matched by the attendee links) or for a customer or supplier itself: open
orders and purchase orders, late items and alerts, recent mail and Teams subjects
and dates, payments and balance (finance), open promises, quality issues and the
last meeting's notes when captured. Cited, bounded, no model call. Not found reads
the same as a record you cannot see.

Your briefing: the events routed to you that you may see, ranked by impact; the
top ones each with why, a suggested next action and how we know, every other one
counted in its type's group; each check's state; and a preview of the daily
digest (never sent). ``view=since_visit``: only what is new since your last visit.
One event type's items of your briefing, a page at a time (a group's "+N more").

post.description: Mark your briefing seen now: the next "since your last visit" starts here.

Dismiss or snooze one item the AI watcher flagged in your briefing (``open``
undoes it). Only your own briefing changes; nothing is sent.

get.description:
The link explorer: a record's neighbours one hop out, grouped by kind of link,
capped per kind, as this reader may see them. Walk on by asking for a neighbour.
Not found reads the same as a record the reader cannot see.

Your feedback, newest first; the owner and the admins see every reader's (an
admin who is not the owner reads another reader's answer as their own markings
allow).

post.description:
Rate an answer you were given: up or down, what was wrong, the claims that were
wrong and the right answer, kept as you saw the answer. The rating and its record
are one write: when either fails, neither is kept.

A briefing or alert item: useful, not useful or wrong. Not useful or wrong
suppresses it in your briefing (the AI watcher's and the proactive engine's).

A note on a page, a record, a list, the app itself or anything else: general
feedback needs only the note; a page or record is attached when sent.
Triage (the owner and the admins): new, accepted, fixed or won't fix.

get.description:
Every late purchase order you may see, a page at a time, longest late first
(Home shows the first ones: "show all").

A record's Impact panel, read on demand: what a change (a delay of N days, out
of stock, a customer lost, a price change) puts at risk downstream, or why an order
is late or unprofitable. Not found reads the same as a record the reader cannot
see; nothing is written.

One slow section of a record's page (late check, people, landed cost, how we
know), read after its quick first read and merged into it. Not found reads the
same as a record the reader cannot see.

One record's page. ``object_id``: the URL-encoded object id, or a business
reference (e.g. a PO number) resolved within ``object_type``.

parameters.description: A first read without the checks (complete=false), shown while the full page is read
parameters.name: quick

schema.description: A first read without the checks (complete=false), shown while the full page is read
schema.title: Quick

get.description: A cited source as this reader may open it (a Source's open_url page reads it).
Typo-tolerant autocomplete over the records this reader may see.

What needs your attention and what to do: late or unconfirmed purchase orders
and the customer orders they hold up, "ETA confirmed?", customer orders at risk and
margin alerts, ranked by impact; each with how we know, confidence, what is missing,
a draft message and the actions it offers (``/api/actions/*``: nothing is sent
without your confirm).

Your follows, your alert rules and your alerts (newest first), each alert shown
only as far as your grant admits now. Kept in the Workbench, never in a source.

post.description: Mark some of your alerts read.

Follow a record you can open: you are told when it or a record linked to it
changes, and when a new record (a mail, a shipment, an invoice) is linked to it.
Keep the rule you were shown (its spec and digest), validated again.

An alert rule in plain words, compiled into the restricted rule spec and shown
back in plain words for you to confirm; nothing is kept. A rule the grammar cannot
hold, or one over figures your markings do not cover, is refused with the reason.
